paras: It was a rainy morning. Saraswati and her little brother Rama were sitting near the window. Suddenly, the rain stopped and the sun came out. 'Look!' said Saraswati. 'A rainbow!'
Rama clapped his hands. 'It has so many colours! Where does it come from?' he asked. Saraswati smiled. 'Let us find out,' she said.
Saraswati took a small glass of water and put it near the window. The sunlight passed through the water and made tiny rainbow colours on the wall. 'Wow!' said Rama.
'Sunlight looks white,' said Saraswati. 'But it is made of many colours. When light passes through water, it bends and splits into different colours. That is called refraction.'
Later, they went outside. The sky still had tiny water drops floating in the air. 'The rainbow in the sky is made the Ramae way,' said Saraswati.
'The sun shines on the tiny water drops. The light bends inside each drop and splits into seven colours. Then we see a big rainbow in the sky.'
Rama looked up. 'So the sun and water drops work together to make a rainbow,' he said. 'Yes,' said Saraswati. 'That is why we see a rainbow mostly after the rain, when the sun comes out.'
Rama smiled. 'Physics is everywhere!' Saraswati laughed and said, 'Yes, even in the sky!'

items.q: When did Saraswati and Rama see the rainbow?
items.a: They saw it after the rain, when the sun came out.

items.q: What did Saraswati use to make tiny rainbow colours on the wall?
items.a: She used a small glass of water and sunlight.

items.q: What happens when sunlight passes through water?
items.a: The light bends and splits into many colours.

items.q: Why do we mostly see a rainbow after the rain?
items.a: Because after the rain, there are tiny water drops in the air, and the sun shines on them to make a rainbow.

sections.heading: B. Match the word with its meaning.

items.r: Bending of light when it passes through water.
Seven colours seen in the sky after rain.
White light made of many colours.
Tiny bits of water in the air that split sunlight.
